findings.title: User verification skipped when Integration does not yet exist
findings.body: When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the view returns next_step() before the github_authenticated_user check runs. An attacker can supply any installation_id that has no webhook-created row yet and complete the pipeline without proving they installed it. build_integration fetches installation info and creates the integration anyway. The sender check is only enforced when a webhook-created row already exists, so the protection is bypassable.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the key exists. Integrations created through the pipeline, or older ones created before sender was stored, have no sender key. This raises a 500 instead of rendering the error page.

findings.title: OAuth redirect URL parameters not URL-encoded
findings.body: The redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode. The redirect_uri contains ':' and '/' characters and may contain query characters, which can corrupt the request to GitHub. Use urlencode to build the query string.

findings.title: get_user_info failures not handled
findings.body: get_user_info makes an HTTP call to GitHub. If GitHub returns an error or the call raises, the exception is not caught and the user sees a 500 instead of the friendly error page. safe_urlopen at line 423 is also outside the try block, so network errors there are unhandled too.
